messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High GPU queue growth detected for cluster 'eu-gpu-prod' — queue_len > 95% for 3m, HPA not scaling (custom-metrics-adapter errors). Paging oncall-sre.

sasha: @oncall-sre I'm getting 500s from the metrics adapter when hitting /metrics/custom. HPA shows stable replica count but queue is spiking.

mike: seeing same in dashboards — queued requests for 'inference-pool-gpu' up 8x in 10m. Token throughput flat, latency rising.

lee: any recent deploys to the adapter or prometheus scrape configs?

jordan: nothing on adapter from deploy log, but prom-scrape logs show timeout to adapter endpoints around 3419876510.

rahul: I can repro adapter 503s locally hitting the custom metrics endpoint. Stack traces show DB connection pool exhaustion on the adapter side.

oncall-sre: I'm looking. For mitigation we should either (A) scale the deployment behind the adapter, (B) reconfigure HPA to use alternative metric (queue length), or (C) manually scale GPU pool to soak traffic. Which is least risky?

sasha: (C) + (B) temporarily. If adapter is blackholing metrics, HPA won't react. Manually scale GPU nodes by adding 4 pods to 'inference-pool-gpu' to buy time.

mike: agreed. I'll kick off manual scale. kubectl -n prod scale deploy inference-pool-gpu --replicas=12

deploy-bot: deploy accepted: inference-pool-gpu -> replicas=12 by mike at 2026-03-15T14:10:04Z

jordan: after scale started, queue length plateaued but latency still elevated. Some customers report 429 throttles from front door.

sasha: which customers? need impact scope for incident report.

mike: customer-support: two enterprise customers (org-acme, org-spark) opened high-priority tickets showing 429s and delayed responses starting ~14:05Z. Also internal synthetic checks failing.

lee: I can flip HPA metric to use internal queue-exporter temporarily. Patch: kubectl -n prod patch hpa inference-pool-gpu --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/metrics/0/metricName","value":"inference_queue_length"}]'

rahul: hold — if adapter is down we may need to point to the queue-exporter which is a direct exporter on the deployment. I'll validate metric name.

oncall-sre: Meanwhile I'm restarting the custom-metrics-adapter pod to clear connection pool. kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/custom-metrics-adapter

incident-bot: ACTION: restart initiated for deployment/custom-metrics-adapter by oncall-sre at 3419876568

jordan: adapter restarted; logs show adapter warmed up but then throwing 502 upstream on DB calls. Might be a different downstream service.

rahul: I can scale the adapter horizontally: kubectl -n monitoring scale deploy custom-metrics-adapter --replicas=4. That should reduce per-pod load while we debug DB issue.

deploy-bot: deploy accepted: custom-metrics-adapter -> replicas=4 by rahul at 2026-03-15T14:14:20Z

mike: after adapter scale we see adapter 200s and HPA metrics flowing again. HPA reconciler still shows old target, triggering slow growth; I think HPA controller has backoff due to prior errors.

sasha: can we force HPA controller to re-evaluate? kubectl -n prod annotate hpa inference-pool-gpu hpa.kubernetes.io/recheck=\"$(date +%s)\"

lee: annotation applied. HPA now picked up new metrics and is initiating scale to target of 18 replicas.

oncall-sre: Good — queue is draining, token latency dropping. Customer tickets showing fewer 429s. Marking impact: degraded for 21 minutes, affecting subset of enterprise customers (org-acme, org-spark), synthetic checks.

jordan: root cause: custom-metrics-adapter DB connection pool exhaustion + adapter errors created a metrics blackhole. HPA didn't get metrics -> no autoscale -> GPU pool exhausted -> requests queued and throttled.

rahul: follow-up immediate fixes: increase adapter DB pool size, add circuit-breaker and better retry on adapter, add prometheus alert for adapter 5xx > 5m, and add a fallback HPA metric that uses queue-exporter when custom metrics are unavailable.

sasha: operations notes for postmortem: timeline, customers impacted, commands executed (scale inference-pool-gpu -> 12, scale adapter -> 4, annotate hpa recheck), mitigation rationale.

mike: logging snippets I captured: ```
custom-metrics-adapter ERROR DBConnPool: timeout acquiring connection after 30s
kube-controller-manager INFO HPA backoff: metrics unavailable
inference-pool-gpu INFO queue_len=1870 -> throttle triggered
```

oncall-sre: next steps: 1) raise CR to increase DB pool + deploy adapter change (rahul), 2) add HPA fallback metric and test (lee), 3) add runbook step for manual scale for oncall (sasha), 4) follow-up postmortem doc (jordan).

rahul: I'll open the PR for adapter pool size and add a healthcheck endpoint that refuses traffic if DB unavailable. Targeting hotfix in next 24h.

lee: I'll schedule a short runbook session with oncall team to practice manual HPA fallback; also add Grafana panel for queue-exporter metric with an alert.

jordan: I'll stitch timeline and customer impact and start the postmortem doc; assign to ops and eng for follow-ups.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated at 3419876625 — queue draining, HPA reconnected, adapter scaled. Impact window ~3419876410 - 3419876625 (~3.6m of high degradation, 21m total customer-visible).

sasha: thanks team. I'll stay on until metrics are stable for 30m then hand off.

oncall-sre: handing off to sasha for watch. If queue reappears -> full escalation.

mike: closing temporary manual scales and keeping autoscale active. Will revert any non-configurable manual changes postmortem.

jordan: postmortem draft created: /docs/incidents/3419876543-postmortem-draft.md — please add notes and timeline entries.

sasha: noted. tagging @support to update impacted customer threads.

rahul: PR opened for adapter fixes: github.com/redwood-inference/custom-metrics-adapter/pull/482

lee: adding runbook entry now.

incident-bot: CLOSED: incident moved to monitoring state; watch oncall: sasha.

sasha: thanks everyone. I'll update incident channel if anything else pops up.
